# Current Recommended Next.js Architecture for New Production Apps — Current vs Legacy

**Scope:** Current guidance as of Next.js 16.x (docs version 16.3.5, last updated 2026-07-21 to 2026-08-25). All recommendations below are verified against official Next.js docs and current 2026 migration guidance.

## 1. Router choice: App Router is the current default

For a new production application, use **App Router (`app/` directory)**. `create-next-app` labels App Router as “(recommended)” and includes it in recommended defaults with TypeScript, Tailwind, ESLint, and Turbopack ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)).

**Legacy / version-specific distinction:**

- **Current:** `app/` folder-based routing for all new projects.
- **Legacy but still supported:** Pages Router (`pages/` directory). It still ships in Next.js 16, is **not deprecated**, and has no removal date announced — it is maintained for existing apps ([App vs Pages Guide](https://arc.dev/employer-blog/nextjs-app-router-vs-pages-router/)).
- Do not start a new app on Pages Router to avoid a future migration unless there is an extreme tight-deadline familiarity constraint. For existing Pages apps, incremental coexistence (`app/` + `pages/` in one project, `app` prioritized) is supported, with hard navigation between routers.

## 2. Data-fetching and rendering: Server-first, not page-level data functions

**Current model:** fetch directly in async Server Components using `fetch` or ORM/database access. Identical `fetch` requests in the tree are memoized per render. `fetch` is **not cached by default** — use `use cache` to cache or wrap in `Suspense` / `loading.js` to stream fresh data at request time ([Fetching Data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data)).

Mutations belong in **Server Actions**; external/webhook/mobile REST needs belong in **Route Handlers**. Server Actions are POST-only with no GET caching and are not recommended for reads — prefer Server Components or Route Handlers for cacheable reads ([Data Patterns](https://github.com/vercel/nextjs-skills/blob/main/skills/next-best-practices/data-patterns.md)).

**Legacy mapping — do not use in new `app/` code** ([Migration Guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration)):

| Legacy (Pages-only) | Current (App Router) |
|---|---|
| `getServerSideProps` | `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })` / uncached + `Suspense`, or `headers()`/`cookies()` in Server Component |
| `getStaticProps` | `fetch(..., { cache: 'force-cache' })` or `use cache` |
| `getStaticProps + revalidate` | `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: N } })` |
| `getStaticPaths` + `fallback` | `generateStaticParams` + `dynamicParams` |
| `pages/api/*` | `route.js` Route Handlers |
| `pages/_app.js` / `_document.js` | Single `app/layout.js` root layout with `<html>`/`<body>` |
| `pages/_error.js`, `pages/404.js`, `next/head`, `next/router` | `error.js`, `not-found.js`, Metadata API, `next/navigation` (`useRouter`, `usePathname`, `useSearchParams`) |

## 3. Structure, Server/Client boundary, and caching

**Structure (current):** nested folders define routes; `page.js` makes a segment public; `layout.js` defines shared UI that persists across navigation; root layout is required ([Migration Guide](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration)).

**Server/Client Components (current):** layouts and pages are Server Components by default. Use Client Components only when you need state/event handlers, `useEffect`, browser APIs, or custom hooks — declared with `"use client"` at the top. To reduce client JS, push `"use client"` to specific interactive leaves, not whole layouts; pass Server Components as `children`/props into Client Components ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

**Caching (current):** opt-in **Cache Components** enabled by `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`, with `use cache` directive for data- or component-level caching and Partial Prerendering. `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerender model. If not using Cache Components, docs label the older fetch/ISR behavior as “Previous Model” — treat automatic static caching assumptions from pre-16 tutorials as outdated ([Caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching)).

### Practical starter for new prod app

- `create-next-app@latest --yes` (App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, ESLint, Turbopack) ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation))
- `app/layout.tsx` + `app/page.tsx`, nested `layout.tsx`/`page.tsx`, `loading.tsx`/`error.tsx`, `route.ts` only for public API
- Async Server Components for reads with explicit caching; Server Actions for forms/mutations with `revalidatePath/Tag`; SWR/React Query only for truly client-side reads
- `generateStaticParams` for static dynamic routes; `force-static`/`no-store` set explicitly per segment

## Remaining uncertainty

None critical. Minor version churn (e.g., Cache Components defaults evolving across 15→16) means always read docs for the installed Next.js version, not generic 2023-2024 tutorials that assume automatic fetch caching.

# OpenCut Official Automation Interfaces — Released vs Roadmap vs Third-Party vs Not-Found

## Bottom line

**OpenCut currently provides zero officially released automation interfaces.** No public REST API, SDK, CLI, webhooks, MCP server, plugin/extension API, scripting interface, or headless/batch mode was found as a released, supported offering. The official project explicitly frames all five automation-adjacent capabilities as forthcoming rewrite work, current official docs contain no automation surface, and a community proposal corroborates that OpenCut “lacks a programmatic entry point” ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut), [docs](https://opencut.dev/), [Issue #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778)).

What does exist falls into two other buckets:

- **Official roadmap + open community proposals** — not released, not merged.
- **Third-party Playwright-based MCP bridges** — functional but unofficial, local-only, and tied to the archived classic codebase.

## 1. Released official interfaces: none found

The [official README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut) on `main` states:

> “OpenCut is being rewritten from the ground up. What’s coming: An Editor API … First-class third party plugins … MCP server (for AI agents) … Headless mode (automation, batch rendering) … A scripting tab directly in the editor”

That wording places Editor API, plugins, MCP server, headless mode, and scripting tab in the future, not in released features.

The [official documentation](https://opencut.dev/) corroborates the absence: features are listed as timeline-based editing, multi-track support, real-time preview, no subscriptions, and cross-platform support, with a project structure of `apps/web`, `apps/desktop`, `src/components`, `stores`, `hooks`, and `lib` — no API/CLI/SDK/webhook/MCP/plugin section.

Community proposal [Issue #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778) independently states the same gap:

> “OpenCut today is a polished in-browser editor, but it lacks a programmatic entry point … AI agents cannot drive OpenCut … OpenCut cannot be embedded into other products … without spinning up a real browser.”

Conclusion: treat any claim of a current official OpenCut REST API, CLI, SDK, MCP endpoint, plugin registry, or headless renderer as unsupported.

## 2. Official roadmap material (not released)

The maintainer-authored tracker [Tracking: OpenCut rewrite #811](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811), opened May 26, 2026 and still Open, defines the official automation roadmap:

What’s coming:

- **Editor API:** “a clean, stable API anyone can build on top of”
- **Plugin system:** third-party plugins, including mobile
- **MCP server:** “for AI agents”
- **Headless mode:** “automation, batch rendering, CI pipelines”
- **Scripting tab:** “write and run scripts directly inside the editor”

Architectural precondition stated in the same issue: separating a shared Rust core (engine) from Web/Desktop/Android/iOS UIs, with MCP, headless, and scripting all consuming that core.

Status:

- Progress checklist items — Engine Core, Editor API design, Plugin API design, Plugin host, Project storage, Web UI, Headless mode, MCP server, Scripting, Desktop UI, Android/iOS, Public beta — are unchecked.
- No timeline or release date is given.
- The [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut) points users to `opencut-classic` / production for usable editing while the rewrite lives separately until takeover.

Therefore these five items are **roadmap, not released interfaces**.

## 3. Community proposals and RFCs (not official, not merged)

Three automation proposals were found, all community-authored and none merged as an official release:

### a) Headless Rendering SDK + Visual Config UI — [Issue #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778)

- Open enhancement by `lfzm`, filed Apr 27, 2026, label `enhancement`, state Open, no linked branches/PRs.
- Proposes new `@opencut/render-sdk` Library API (`import { render }`), CLI (`opencut-render run draft.json -o out.mp4`), Playwright-driven headless Chromium, `RenderServer` batch class, plus `@opencut/config-ui` visual template editor and opt-in `apps/web/src/automation/` bridge (`DraftTemplate` zod schema, compiler to `SerializedProject`, `window.__opencutAutomation` gated by `NEXT_PUBLIC_AUTOMATION=1`).
- Explicitly asks: “Is this direction welcome upstream?” and notes a working prototype on a local fork (76/76 unit tests, end-to-end render verified).
- Attribution: **community proposal, not an official interface**.

### b) Portable project file for programmatic workflows — [Issue #719](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719)

- Open enhancement by `quochuydev`, filed Mar 5, 2026, state Open.
- States: “OpenCut has no portable project file format. Projects are locked in IndexedDB/OPFS … external tools (AI assistants, CLI scripts, automation pipelines) have no way to programmatically generate an editing project.”
- Proposes documented versioned `.json` format, export/import buttons, filename-referenced media, and published JSON Schema for external generators.
- Referenced by open PR #764; issue itself remains Open.
- Attribution: **community feature request, not a released format**.

### c) MCP server + WebSocket bridge — [PR #752](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/pull/752)

- Community PR by `oijofie`, opened Mar 26, 2026, state **Closed without merge** into `OpenCut-app:main`.
- Added `packages/mcp-server` and `packages/ws-bridge` with 9 tools (`get_timeline`, `split`, `remove_range`, `trim`, `undo`, `redo`, `seek`, `play`, `pause`), browser-side `useWsBridge` hook, and `CLAUDE.md`.
- Attribution: **closed community attempt, not adopted as official**.

Related demand signals (Python API requests, API/CLI/headless-for-agents requests, local-first agent-bridge RFCs) follow the same pattern: open requests acknowledging no current entry point. They do not create an official interface.

## 4. Third-party interfaces (functional but unofficial)

The only working automation found lives **outside `OpenCut-app`** and uses Playwright injection into a locally patched editor. Do not present these as official:

### JXUE0/opencut-controller — [repo](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller)

- Owner `JXUE0`, not `OpenCut-app`.
- Advertises 161 MCP tools, dual `stdio` / HTTP-streamable transport, Playwright integration, contextual resources (`opencut://projects`, `opencut://editor/state`, `opencut://timeline/tracks`), and pre-built prompts.
- Requires legacy Next.js App Router build: clone archived `opencut-classic`, run `pnpm run patch-editor ../opencut-classic`, and run the editor locally.
- Explicitly local-only: production does not expose internal hooks, so “You must run the OpenCut editor locally.”

### RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP — [repo](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP)

- Owner `RavenMeld`; credited by the JXUE0 project as the foundational work it builds on.
- Same pattern: 161 tools, headless Chromium via Playwright, `page.evaluate()` calls into `EditorCore` / Zustand stores via `window.__opencut` and `window.__stores`, requiring two small patches to `editor-provider.tsx` and `projects/page.tsx`.

### kenimo49/opencut-mcp — [repo](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp)

- Explicitly “does not target” upstream `opencut-classic` (archived); targets the `kenimo49/opencut-classic` fork with patches `eca73042` (exposes `window.__editor`) and `a7443ec8` (time-tick helpers).
- Status self-described as “PoC for a kenimoto.dev article series,” pinned to fork commit `a7443ec8`, not semver.
- Tools: `opencut_get_state`, `add_media`, `insert_clip`, `split_at`, `move`/`trim`/`delete`, `undo`/`redo`, `export`, `screenshot`.

Distinguishing rule: **ownership outside `OpenCut-app` + required source patch + local classic/fork runtime + no production support = third-party**, even when tool counts overlap.

## 5. Not-found evidence (why “none released” is a researched absence)

- [Official docs navigation](https://opencut.dev/) lists only Code of Conduct, Contributing, Development, Getting Help, Getting Started, Security, Transcription Service, plus Troubleshooting FAQs (fonts, Bun cache, Vercel deploy, OPFS Safari, ffmpeg WASM, Postgres, background remover, auth secrets) — no API/CLI/SDK/MCP/plugin/webhook/headless page.
- The [Mintlify `llms.txt` API index](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/llms.txt) documents only in-process primitives — `EditorCore` singleton, `TimelineManager`, `ScenesManager`, `ProjectManager`, `RendererManager`, `Actions`, `Commands`, `CommandManager`, `useEditor()` / `useEditorActions()` — accessed via `EditorCore.getInstance()` or React hooks inside the web app, not an external automation contract.
- The [original codebase repo](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic) was archived by the owner on May 17, 2026, now read-only: “archived and no longer maintained. The rewrite is happening at opencut-app/opencut.” Classic-era internals that third-party bridges patch are therefore frozen, not a current official surface.

No contradiction requiring resolution was found; roadmap language, proposal text, docs absence, and third-party local-only limits all point the same way.

## Practical guidance

- If you need a **supported official automation contract today**, there is none to pin, version, or depend on.
- If tracking the future, watch [Issue #811](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811) and the `main` [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut) for Engine Core → Editor API → Plugin/MCP/Headless/Scripting progression.
- If experimenting, use third-party bridges ([JXUE0](https://github.com/JXUE0/opencut-controller), [RavenMeld](https://github.com/RavenMeld/OpenCut-MCP), [kenimo49](https://github.com/kenimo49/opencut-mcp)) only with the understanding that they require patched local classic/fork editors, break with upstream drift, and are not official or production-supported.
- If designing integrations, note [Issue #719](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/719) (portable JSON) and [Issue #778](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/778) (SDK/CLI/template schema) are still proposals; do not treat `DraftTemplate`, `window.__opencutAutomation`, `window.__opencut`, or `window.__editor` as stable official contracts.

# Can you install a usable official OpenCut desktop app on macOS today? — No

**Direct answer:** No. There is no usable official OpenCut desktop application for macOS to download and install today. The first-party desktop project is explicitly early and non-functional as an editor. What first-party OpenCut offers today that is usable is the web version. macOS `.dmg` / one-click-install claims belong to a separately-named third-party fork, not to official OpenCut distribution.

## 1. First-party availability: no official macOS desktop build

First-party sources state the official desktop app is not a usable product:

- The official desktop README describes OpenCut Desktop as built with GPUI and warns: “Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens.” The only documented actions are developer run/check/build commands, not installation of a packaged app: https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md
- The official v0.3.0 release notes likewise describe `apps/desktop/` as “a new GPUI + Rust app” that is early with only `main.rs` and a working build setup, “but no features yet”: https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases
- The official homepage, https://opencut.app/, presents OpenCut as working on any platform with a “Try early beta” / Projects web flow; it lists no macOS `.dmg` / `.app` download.

Conclusion: first-party availability for a usable macOS desktop editor is absent.

## 2. Official installation method on macOS: source/dev only, not usable

There is no official packaged macOS installer documented:

- The official main README says OpenCut is being rewritten, that https://opencut.app/ still runs the classic version “which is the one to reach for today,” and that the rewrite will live elsewhere until ready: https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md
- The documented official run methods are source/dev commands — `moon run web:dev`, `api:dev`, `desktop:dev` — not a downloadable installer: https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md
- For the desktop path on macOS, the stated requirement is Xcode command line tools for the Metal renderer, with `cargo run / check / build --release`; the first build compiles GPUI from source and takes a while: https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md

Practical meaning: on macOS you can clone/build the repo for development, but that desktop build only opens a test window. For actual editing through official channels, use the web classic version.

## 3. Third-party vs first-party: where the macOS .dmg claim comes from

The macOS one-click-install claim is third-party:

- A different GitHub organization, `opencut-desktop-app/opencut`, advertises Windows `.exe`, Mac `OpenCut.dmg` “drag to Applications” claimed as notarized universal for Apple Silicon + Intel, and Linux `.deb / .rpm / AppImage`: https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut/blob/main/README.md
- That same repo explicitly states it is “a packaged build and AI-extended fork of OpenCut (`OpenCut-app/OpenCut`)” and an “Independent project — not affiliated with the OpenCut core team”: https://github.com/opencut-desktop-app/opencut/blob/main/README.md

Distinguishing rule: `OpenCut-app/OpenCut` = first-party; `opencut-desktop-app/opencut` = third-party repackager/fork despite the similar name. Do not treat its `.dmg` as evidence of official macOS availability, signing, notarization, or support.

## Practical guidance

- If you need official and usable today on macOS: use the browser at https://opencut.app/ or run the official web app from source; do not expect a desktop `.app`.
- If you consider the third-party `.dmg`: evaluate it as unaffiliated third-party software with its own trust, update, and AI-data-handling implications, not as the official app.
- Note: live re-fetch of the third-party README returned an error during research while search-index snippets retained its claims/disclaimer, so treat that third-party distribution as potentially volatile; verify the release page and checksums before trusting any download.

# OpenCut Architecture & Technology Stack — Classic vs Rewrite vs Current vs Roadmap

## TL;DR / Generation split

Do not read OpenCut sources as one stack. Use generation + date:

- **Classic (production current):** browser-first local-first Next.js editor still serving `opencut.app`; code now frozen at `opencut-classic`, archived May 17, 2026 ([classic repo header](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic)).
- **Rewrite (development current):** `OpenCut-app/OpenCut` `main` mid-2026 is a Moon/Vite/Elysia/GPUI scaffold with Rust core, Editor API, plugins, MCP, headless still planned; preview at `new.opencut.app` ([rewrite README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)).
- **Roadmap:** unchecked engine/API/plugin/host/storage/UI/headless/MCP/scripting/GPUI-desktop/mobile/beta list with no firm date; takeover plan moves old editor to `old.opencut.app` with project carry-over ([tracking issue](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

## 1. Classic generation

Classic is a Turborepo + Bun monorepo with `apps/web` as Next.js application, documented as EditorCore singleton plus Zustand UI state and actions/commands patterns ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

Frontend late-classic: Next.js 16.1.3, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 4, Radix, Zustand 5.0.2, Motion ([classic web package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic/main/apps/web/package.json)), consistent with Next.js 16 / React 19 / Tailwind 4 / Radix / Zustand / Motion in docs ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

Editor/render evolution within classic:

- Early: FFmpeg.wasm + WaveSurfer.js + HTML Canvas preview, local-first privacy, refactor to binary rendering in progress ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).
- Late: mediabunny 1.29.1 + `opencut-wasm` 0.2.10 + wavesurfer 7.9.8, OpenNext Cloudflare deploy ([classic web package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic/main/apps/web/package.json)).
- v0.3.0 Apr 15, 2026 replaced WebGL with Rust/wgpu compositor compiled to WASM (`compositor`/`effects`/`masks`/`gpu`/`time` crates, `rust/wasm` bindings via `src/lib/wasm`) alongside masks, graph keyframes, volume/speed, stickers ([v0.3.0 notes](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases/tag/v0.3.0)).

Storage/backend: IndexedDB for projects/settings + OPFS for media, FFmpeg.js + background-removal + transcription services in early diagram ([early docs](https://opencut.dev/)); Postgres + Drizzle ORM + Redis/Upstash + Better Auth in late stack ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)) ([classic web package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic/main/apps/web/package.json)).

Status: labeled Original OpenCut codebase, archived and unmaintained; rewrite lives at `opencut-app/opencut` ([classic repo header](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic)).

## 2. Rewrite generation — how it differs

Motive is explicit engine/UI split: Web, Desktop, Android, iOS share one Rust core engine; MCP, headless, scripting also consume that core ([tracking issue](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)).

## 3. Current (mid-2026) — prod vs dev

Production current remains classic at `opencut.app`; development current is rewrite scaffold previewed at `new.opencut.app` until takeover ([rewrite README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)). ## 4. Roadmap & source disagreements (resolved)

Roadmap items: finish Rust engine/UI split, Editor + Plugin APIs, plugin host/sandbox/lifecycle, project storage, web UI refresh (grouping, transitions/filters, captions, keyboard-first, larger effects), headless/MCP/scripting, GPUI desktop + mobile, beta with `opencut.app` takeover and `old.opencut.app` fallback, no timeline ([tracking issue](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/issues/811)). Exact storage/auth/media pipeline for rewrite is not yet fixed in checked-in code (core crate unwired, API only health/echo scaffold per July analysis). # Node.js 24: Test Runner, Fetch, and Permission Model — Official-Evidence Status

**Scope:** Current Node.js 24 (v24.x LTS, checked against v24.21.0 docs and v24.0.0 release notes) status of three built-ins: `node:test` test runner, global `fetch`, and Permission Model. All status claims use official Node.js / Undici sources. Version-specific caveats are kept separate per feature.

## 1. Built-in Test Runner (`node:test`)

**Status in Node.js 24: Stable core — Stability: 2 - Stable.**

The v24.x Test runner docs show History: Added in v18.0.0 / v16.17.0, with “The test runner is now stable” in v20.0.0, and header Stability: 2 - Stable (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html).

**What changed in v24:**

- Automatic waiting for subtests: the v24.0.0 release notes state “The test runner module now automatically waits for subtests to finish, eliminating the need to manually await test promises,” contributed in #56664 (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0). The underlying commits are SEMVER-MAJOR: remove promises returned by `test()` / `t.test()` and automatically wait for subtests.
- This is a behavior/breaking-change caveat when migrating from older versions where manual `await t.test(...)` was required.

**Version-specific caveats — kept separate from stable core:**

Newer test-runner sub-features documented in the same v24.x page carry their own lower stability, not the core Stable label (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html):

- Global setup/teardown — Added in v24.0.0, Stability 1.0 Early development
- Randomizing execution order (`--test-randomize` / `--test-random-seed`) — Added in v24.16.0, Stability 1.0 Early development
- Test tags (`tags`, `testTagFilters` / `--experimental-test-tag-filter`) — Added in v24.19.0, Stability 1.0 Early development
- Watch mode — Stability 1 Experimental

Do not treat these sub-features as Stable merely because `node:test` core is Stable.

## 2. Built-in Fetch API

**Status in Node.js 24: Stable — not experimental.**

The v24.x Globals docs for `fetch` show History: v21.0.0 “No longer experimental,” v18.0.0 “No longer behind `--experimental-fetch`,” Added in v17.5.0 / v16.15.0. Implementation is based on Undici, with bundled version checkable via `process.versions.undici` (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/globals.html).

Related `Request`, `Response`, `Headers`, `FormData` globals share the same v21.0.0 “No longer experimental” history in v24 docs.

**What changed in v24:**

- Node.js 24 includes Undici 7, “which brings numerous improvements to the HTTP client capabilities, including better performance and support for newer HTTP features” (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0).
- Official Undici version mapping: Node.js v24.x bundles Undici ~7.x with note “`fetch` is stable; env-proxy support via `--use-env-proxy`,” contrasted with v18.x ~5.x experimental and v20.x ~6.x stable (https://undici.nodejs.org/best-practices/undici-vs-builtin-fetch).

**Version-specific caveats — kept separate:**

- Env-proxy support for built-in `fetch` in v24.0.0+ / v22.21.0+ via `--use-env-proxy` flag (or `NODE_USE_ENV_PROXY=1`) is the v24-specific fetch caveat; programmatic proxy control still uses Undici `ProxyAgent` / dispatcher API.
- Bundled Undici version matters: for fixes/features newer than the bundled ~7.x, install `undici` from npm; check `process.versions.undici` rather than assuming latest Undici behavior.

## 3. Permission Model (`--permission`)

**Status in Node.js 24 docs: Stable — Stability: 2 - Stable.**

The v24.x Permissions docs show History: v23.5.0 / v22.13.0 “This feature is no longer experimental,” Added in v20.0.0, Stability: 2 - Stable, behind flag `--permission` (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/permissions.html).

**What changed in v24:**

- Flag rename in v24.0.0 (SEMVER-MAJOR #56240): “The experimental Permission Model introduced in Node.js 20 has been improved, and the flag has been changed from `--experimental-permission` to simply `--permission`, indicating its increasing stability and readiness for broader adoption” (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0).
- Important dating nuance: the “no longer experimental” docs milestone is recorded as v23.5.0 / v22.13.0, while the v24.0.0 release announcement still used “experimental … improved” language while announcing the rename. Use docs History for stability dating and release notes for flag-rename dating; do not conflate them.

**Version-specific caveats — kept separate:**

Documented in v24.x Permissions docs (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/permissions.html):

- Two modes: Enforce (default with `--permission`, denies with `ERR_ACCESS_DENIED`) vs Audit (with `--permission-audit`, publishes via `node:diagnostics_channel`, does not deny; `--permission` takes precedence if both supplied).
- Constraints: does not inherit to worker threads; restricts fs (via `node:fs`), child_process, worker_threads, native addons, WASI, inspector, OpenSSL STORE loaders; initialized after env setup so `--env-file` / `--openssl-config` / runtime V8 flags are exempt; OpenSSL engines and sqlite loadable extensions blocked; existing fds bypass; `node:sqlite` fs access not guaranteed to be covered.
- Limitations: symlinks are followed even outside granted paths — ensure granted paths contain no relative symlinks.
- The model is described as “seat belt” for trusted code, not a security boundary against malicious code.

## Sources Used

- v24.x Test runner docs (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/test.html)
- v24.x Globals / fetch docs (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/globals.html)
- v24.x Permissions docs (https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v24.x/api/permissions.html)
- Node.js 24.0.0 release notes (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.0.0)
- Undici built-in-fetch version table (https://undici.nodejs.org/best-practices/undici-vs-builtin-fetch)

No material contradictions found; all stability labels taken directly from History/Stability headers, not inferred.

# OpenCut Repository Architecture and Technology Stack — Current Main vs Version-Specific Material

## Scope and method
Researched from official project documentation and the smallest relevant set of source files on `main` as of September 2026. Current rewrite state is taken from the [README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md), [apps/ tree](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/tree/main/apps), [root Cargo.toml](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/Cargo.toml), [apps/web package.json](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/web/package.json), [apps/api package.json](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/api/package.json), [apps/desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md), and [.prototools](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/.prototools). Classic/transitional material is contrasted via [Mintlify Architecture docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture) and [opencut-classic README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic/blob/main/README.md).

## 1. Current repository architecture (main — rewrite in progress)

Current `main` is a Moon + proto monorepo in early rewrite, **not** the classic Turborepo/Next.js editor:

* Top level contains `apps/api`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web` — no `bg-remover/transcription` or `packages/ui,env` at top level in current listing ([apps/ tree](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/tree/main/apps)).
* Rust workspace `version 0.1.0, edition 2024, MIT` with member `apps/desktop` and dependency `gpui 0.2.2` ([root Cargo.toml](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/Cargo.toml)).
* Entry points after `proto use`: `moon run web:dev — localhost:5173`, `moon run api:dev — localhost:8787`, `moon run desktop:dev — see apps/desktop/README.md` ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)).
* Desktop tasks map to Cargo: `desktop:dev=cargo run`, `desktop:check=cargo check`, `desktop:build=cargo build --release`; explicitly “Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens” with Metal (macOS), Win32+DirectWrite (Windows), Vulkan/Blade + Wayland/X11 (Linux) notes ([apps/desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).

## 2. Current technology stack (minimal source files)

* **apps/web (`@opencut/web`):** Vite 8 + `@vitejs/plugin-react` 6, React 19.2 + react-dom 19.2, TanStack Router/Start (+ SSR-query, router plugin, devtools), Tailwind 4.1.18 + `@tailwindcss/vite`, `radix-ui` + `@base-ui/react` + `shadcn`, Cloudflare `vite-plugin` + `wrangler deploy`, TypeScript 6, Vitest, zod, `vite dev --port 5173` ([apps/web package.json](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/web/package.json)).
* **apps/api (`@opencut/api 0.0.1`):** Elysia on Cloudflare Workers; `wrangler dev / deploy / deploy --dry-run` ([apps/api package.json](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/api/package.json)).
* **apps/desktop:** GPUI 0.2.2 Rust native app (see architecture above) ([root Cargo.toml](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/Cargo.toml), [apps/desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).
* **Tooling/runtime:** Pinned via proto as `moon 2.3.3, bun 1.3.11, rust 1.97.0` ([.prototools](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/.prototools)); orchestration via Moon (`moon run …`), `Cargo.lock` committed.

## 3. Version-specific vs roadmap material

### Version-specific to archived opencut-classic — do NOT attribute to current main
* Turborepo monorepo with `apps/web` (Next.js) + `packages/ui, env` + `turbo.json` + `docker-compose.yml`, and `src/components, core/EditorCore, hooks, lib, services, stores (Zustand), types, utils` ([Mintlify Architecture docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture)).
* Singleton `EditorCore` with managers `command, playback, timeline, scenes, project, media, renderer, save, audio, selection`; `lib/commands/base-command.ts` + `timeline/media/scene` domains ([Mintlify Architecture docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture)).
* Classic stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + Radix + Zustand + Motion; FFmpeg.wasm + WaveSurfer + HTML/Canvas preview; Postgres + Drizzle + Redis + Better Auth; Turborepo + Bun + Biome + Docker ([Mintlify Architecture docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture)).
* Transitional classic structure: `apps/web: Next.js`, `apps/desktop: GPUI (in progress)`, `rust: GPU compositor, effects, masks, WASM bindings — actively migrating business logic from TypeScript`, `docs/` ([opencut-classic README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic/blob/main/README.md)).
* Provenance: “original OpenCut codebase … archived and no longer maintained. The rewrite is happening at opencut-app/opencut” ([opencut-classic README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/opencut-classic/blob/main/README.md)).

### Roadmap / future or early-stage (current main)
* “Being rewritten from the ground up. What’s coming: Editor API, first-class third-party plugins (plugin-first), desktop/mobile/browser from one Rust-core codebase, MCP server, headless mode, scripting tab”; “not set up to take outside contributions yet while architecture is being designed” ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)).
* Deployment split: `opencut.app` still runs classic (the one to reach for today); rewrite will live at `new.opencut.app` until takeover ([README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/README.md)).
* Binary renderer to replace HTML/DOM/Canvas preview for preview/export consistency is “in progress”; contributors told to avoid preview/export work ([Mintlify Architecture docs](https://www.mintlify.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/development/architecture)).
* GPUI desktop window-only state above is early implementation, not a full editor port ([apps/desktop README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/blob/main/apps/desktop/README.md)).

## Minimal source-file set used
`README.md`, `apps/` listing, `Cargo.toml`, `apps/web/package.json`, `apps/api/package.json`, `apps/desktop/README.md`, `.prototools` — supplemented only by official docs (Mintlify) and `opencut-classic/README.md` for version labeling, per request to keep source files minimal.

## Remaining uncertainty
No open contradictions. `opencut.dev` dated Sept 2025 (Bun/Docker/Postgres/Redis/Tauri/FFmpeg/Zustand) describes classic and should not be used for current-main stack without checking `main` files first. Rust `crates/*` layout beyond `apps/desktop` and WASM package evolution was not enumerated to respect minimal-file constraint.

# OpenCut — Current Architecture and Technology Stack

## Scope: rewrite vs. classic

The `main` branch of `opencut-app/opencut` is an early ground-up rewrite, distinct from the production codebase users run today. The rewrite is described as plugin-first with a planned shared Rust core, Editor API, MCP server, headless mode, and scripting tab, while the previous version is frozen as `opencut-app/opencut-classic` ([OpenCut main README](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut)).

This distinction matters because much public architecture documentation still describes the classic lineage. This report labels each finding as **current rewrite** or **classic** and stops where rewrite evidence runs out.

## 1. Repository structure and high-level organization

**Current rewrite:** a Moon + proto + Cargo workspace. The root contains `.moon`, `moon.yml`, `.prototools`, `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock`, `bunfig.toml`, `apps/`, `brand/marks`, and `changelog` ([OpenCut main README](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut)).

It contains three apps run through Moon:

- `apps/web`, `apps/api`, `apps/desktop`
- `moon run web:dev` on port 5173, `moon run api:dev` on port 8787, `moon run desktop:dev`, after `proto use` installs pinned tools ([OpenCut main README](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut))

**Architectural direction:** one UI shell per platform over a shared core. The rewrite promises desktop, mobile, and browser from one Rust core codebase with first-class plugins ([OpenCut main README](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut)). No `rust/` shared-core tree was present in the fetched current root listing; the workspace `Cargo.toml` currently members only `apps/desktop`, so the shared Rust core should be treated as planned rather than landed.

## 2. Runtime and core technology stack

### Current rewrite runtime

Pinned toolchain via proto is Moon 2.3.3, Bun 1.3.11, Rust 1.97.0 ([pinned toolchain](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/.prototools)).

- **Web:** Vite 8 with TanStack Start / TanStack Router, React 19.2 + React DOM, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4.1 via the Vite plugin, plus the Cloudflare Vite plugin and Wrangler deploy ([web package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/web/package.json)). Hosting is Cloudflare Workers with entry `@tanstack/react-start/server-entry` and route for the new rewrite domain ([web Workers config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/web/wrangler.jsonc)).
- **API:** Elysia on Cloudflare Workers, using `wrangler dev` / `wrangler deploy` with Workers types and entry `src/index.ts` ([api package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/api/package.json)).
- **Desktop:** Rust binary `opencut-desktop` built with GPUI 0.2.2 from workspace dependencies ([desktop manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/desktop/Cargo.toml)).

### Classic production stack (context)

The documented classic editor processed video locally in the browser with FFmpeg.wasm, used WaveSurfer.js for waveforms, and rendered preview with HTML/Canvas while refactoring toward binary rendering; backend was PostgreSQL + Drizzle ORM + Redis + Better Auth with a repository pattern ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

Persistence was local-first: IndexedDB for projects and settings and OPFS for media files, with import stored to OPFS and export flowing through FFmpeg to download ([OpenCut docs diagram](https://opencut.dev/)).

## 3. User interface architecture

### Current rewrite UI

- Styling and primitives: Tailwind CSS 4.1, `radix-ui` and Base-UI primitives, `shadcn` components, `next-themes`, Lucide and HugeIcons icons, plus `cmdk`, `vaul`, `embla-carousel`, `sonner`, and `react-hook-form` with Zod ([web package](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/web/package.json)).
- Routing: TanStack file-based routing with generated `routeTree.gen.ts` and `router.tsx` using intent preload and scroll restoration ([web router](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opencut-app/opencut/main/apps/web/src/router.tsx)).
- Status: minimal shell. `apps/web/src` contains only `components/ui`, `hooks`, `lib`, `routes`, `router.tsx`, `routeTree.gen.ts`, and `styles.css`, with no editor timeline, preview, stores, or core tree yet ([web src listing](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut/tree/main/apps/web/src)).

### Classic editor UI (context)

Classic UI was Next.js 16 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind 4 + Radix + Zustand + Motion ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)). The editor centered on a multi-track timeline canvas for video/audio/overlay tracks and a preview panel, with Zustand stores for editor, timeline, media, and playback state ([OpenCut docs diagram](https://opencut.dev/)). State was layered as an `EditorCore` singleton accessed via `useEditor`, Zustand for UI preferences and panels, and React local state, with user actions flowing through an actions layer and undoable commands ([architecture docs](https://opencut-app-opencut.mintlify.app/development/architecture)).

## Remaining uncertainty

- Current rewrite media engine and persistence beyond Cloudflare Workers hosting are not documented in the fetched sources; classic FFmpeg.wasm and IndexedDB/OPFS behavior should not be assumed ported.
- The shared Rust core / GPU compositor / `opencut-wasm` migration documented for the classic lineage has no confirmed landed equivalent in the current rewrite root beyond the GPUI desktop shell and pinned Rust toolchain.
- No contradiction was recorded; the main risk is conflating classic documentation with the early rewrite.

# Current Recommended Next.js Architecture for a New Production Application

## Summary

For a new production application, start with the **App Router on the current Next.js 16 line**, using `create-next-app` defaults (TypeScript, Tailwind, ESLint, App Router, Turbopack, `@/*` alias). Keep `app/` as a thin routing/composition layer with `page`/`layout`/`loading`/`error`/`not-found`/`route` conventions, organize by area with route groups and colocate non-routable code in private folders. Default to **Server Components**, fetch data server-first, cache explicitly with **`use cache`** when Cache Components are enabled and stream fresh work with **Suspense**, mutate UI-owned data with **Server Actions** and use **Route Handlers** only for real HTTP contracts. Centralize auth in a **server-only Data Access Layer (DAL)** returning minimal DTOs, validate forms server-side with **Zod + `useActionState`**, and deploy as Node/Docker/adapters with `standalone` output and reverse-proxy + shared-cache handling when self-hosting.

## 1. Router and project structure

**Use App Router for greenfield.** Official guidance states: “For new applications, we recommend using the App Router. This router allows you to use React's latest features and is an evolution of the Pages Router” ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)). Next.js documents two routers — “App Router: The newer router that supports new React features like Server Components” and “Pages Router: The original router, still supported” — and advises new projects to use only one router to avoid confusion because `app` takes priority over `pages` ([Docs overview](https://nextjs.org/docs)).

**Start from defaults.** “The default setup enables TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, ESLint, App Router, and Turbopack, with import alias `@/*`” ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)). This is the recommended baseline for production; customize linter, `src/` choice, and React Compiler from there rather than starting minimal.

**File conventions.** “Add `page` to expose a route, `layout` for shared UI such as header, nav, or footer, `loading` for skeletons, `error` for error boundaries, and `route` for APIs” ([Project structure](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)). Folders define URL segments; a folder becomes public only when it contains `page` or `route`.

**Organize without changing URLs.** “Organize code without changing URLs with route groups `(group)`, and colocate non-routable files with private folders `_folder`” ([Project structure](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure)). Practical application:

- `(marketing)`, `(dashboard)`, `(app)` groups for separate layouts/shells with clean URLs (e.g. `app/(marketing)/page.tsx` → `/`).
- `_components`, `_lib` private folders for route-colocated UI and server helpers.
- Keep route files thin orchestrators; shared UI and server logic live outside `app/` in clearly owned modules.
- Do not keep `pages/` alongside `app/` indefinitely after migration; a single router avoids split data-fetching models.

## 2. Rendering, data-fetching, caching, and mutations

### Server vs Client Components

“By default, layouts and pages are Server Components, which lets you fetch data and render parts of your UI on the server, optionally cache the result, and stream it to the client. When you need interactivity or browser APIs, you can use Client Components to layer in functionality” ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

Use Client Components when you need “State and event handlers … Lifecycle logic … Browser-only APIs … Custom hooks”; use Server Components when you need to “Fetch data from databases or APIs close to the source … Use API keys, tokens, and other secrets … Reduce the amount of JavaScript sent to the browser” ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).

Boundary discipline:

- Declare with `"use client"` and “add `'use client'` to specific interactive components instead of marking large parts of your UI as Client Components”; “Props passed to Client Components need to be serializable” ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).
- Server Components can render Client Components; to wrap server-rendered content in an interactive wrapper, pass Server Components as `children`/props rather than importing server code into the client tree.
- Render context providers as deep as possible: “React context is not supported in Server Components. To use context, create a Client Component that accepts `children` … You should render providers as deep as possible in the tree” ([Server and Client Components](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components)).
- Guard boundaries with `server-only` / `client-only` to fail fast on accidental imports.

### Fetching and caching

“Identical `fetch` requests in a React component tree are memoized by default … `fetch` requests are not cached by default … Use the `use cache` directive to cache results, or wrap the fetching component in `Suspense` to stream fresh data at request time” ([Fetching data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data)). For non-`fetch` reads (ORM/DB), deduplicate per request with `React.cache`.

With Cache Components enabled via `cacheComponents: true`, “The `use cache` directive caches the return value of async functions and components … For components that fetch data … and require fresh data on every request, do not use `use cache`. Instead, wrap the component in `Suspense` and provide a fallback UI” ([Caching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/caching)). Consequences for new apps:

- Dynamic by default under Cache Components; opt into caching explicitly.
- Cache data functions/components with `use cache` + lifetime/tags; stream runtime-dependent work with `Suspense`.
- Fetch where data is needed (memoization avoids prop-drilling); parallelize independent reads; place `Suspense` around meaningful slow chunks, not just the whole page.

### Mutations: Server Actions vs Route Handlers

“A Server Action is a React Server Function invoked through React's action mechanisms, such as `forms`, `useActionState`, or a client-side transition … Next.js dispatches Server Actions one at a time per client … When a Server Action triggers an immediate revalidation, Next.js does the work inside one HTTP request: it runs the action, then re-renders the current route server-side” ([Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions)).

Choose invalidation by intent: “`updateTag`: immediate expiration of a tag … `revalidateTag`: stale-while-revalidate refresh … `revalidatePath`: invalidate by URL path … `refresh`: refetch the current route's RSC Payload without invalidating cached data” ([Server Actions](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/server-actions)). Practical rule:

- Server Actions for UI-owned mutations: forms, buttons, toggles, settings; co-locate with the feature, validate + authorize inside, then `updateTag` for read-your-own-writes or `revalidateTag`/`revalidatePath` for background/path updates.
- Route Handlers (`app/**/route.ts`) for HTTP contracts: webhooks, OAuth callbacks, mobile/third-party APIs, cron, cacheable GETs, streaming/SSE, custom status/headers, large binary uploads.
- Treat every Action/Handler as a public entry point: authenticate, authorize (ownership/role), and validate inside; do not rely on page-level checks or hidden `bind` args.

## 3. Production stack: TypeScript, styling, auth/data, forms/state

**TypeScript + styling.** The default setup already enables TypeScript and Tailwind ([Installation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/installation)). For styling, “Use Tailwind CSS for most styling needs … Use CSS Modules for component-specific styles when Tailwind utilities aren't sufficient” ([CSS](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/css)). Keep global/Tailwind imports in the root layout and use CSS Modules or scoped files only for truly custom cases.

**Auth: library + DAL + DTOs.** “While you can implement a custom auth solution, for increased security and simplicity, we recommend using an authentication library” with session management, authorization, social logins, MFA, and RBAC ([Authentication](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/authentication)).

Centralize enforcement: “For new projects, we recommend creating a dedicated Data Access Layer (DAL) … Only run on the server. Perform authorization checks. Return safe, minimal Data Transfer Objects (DTOs) … A page-level authentication check does not extend to the Server Actions defined within it. Always re-verify inside the action … only the Data Access Layer should access `process.env`” ([Data security](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/data-security)). Apply the same pattern to mutations: thin `"use server"` actions delegating to `server-only` DAL functions, with per-resource ownership checks.

**Forms.** “For server-side validation, you can use a schema validation library like Zod or Valibot … To display validation errors or messages, turn the component that defines the form into a Client Component and use React `useActionState`” ([Forms](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/forms)). Production form checklist: shared Zod schema used on both client (UX) and server (truth), `safeParse` + `flatten().fieldErrors`, `(prevState, formData)` signature, inline `role="alert"` errors, `pending`/`useFormStatus` states, and return-values for expected errors rather than throwing for validation/permission failures.

## 4. Deployment, performance, and current version

**Deployment targets.** “Next.js can be deployed as a Node.js server, Docker container, static export, or adapted to run on different platforms … Docker deployments support all Next.js features” ([Deploying](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/deploying)). For containers use `output: "standalone"` multi-stage images and copy `.next/static` + `public/` explicitly.

**Self-hosting.** “When self-hosting, it's recommended to use a reverse proxy (like nginx) in front of your Next.js server … By default, Next.js uses an in-memory cache that is not shared across instances. For consistent caching behavior, use `'use cache: remote'` with a custom cache handler … Set a consistent encryption key using `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` … Configure a `deploymentId`” ([Self-hosting](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting)). Ensure proxies/load balancers pass through streaming (chunked responses) without buffering, otherwise Partial Prerendering/streaming advantages are lost.

**Current line.** “Cache Components are a new set of features … They center around the new `use cache` directive … You can enable Cache Components in your `next.config.ts` file: `cacheComponents: true`” ([Next.js 16](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-16)). Start new production apps on Next.js 16.x with Turbopack; evaluate opt-in `cacheComponents` (and related prefetching flags) deliberately because it changes the caching mental model to dynamic-by-default with explicit caching.

## Recommended starting checklist

1. `create-next-app` with App Router + TypeScript + Tailwind + ESLint + Turbopack + `@/*`.
2. `app/` with `(marketing)`/`(app)` groups, `loading`/`error`/`not-found`, `_components` colocation; no long-lived `pages/`.
3. Server-first pages; `"use client"` only on small leaves; serializable props; deep providers.
4. Server `fetch`/DB reads with memoization; `use cache` for cacheable work, `Suspense` for fresh work.
5. Server Actions for UI mutations + precise invalidation; Route Handlers for webhooks/public APIs/streaming.
6. Auth library + `server-only` DAL + DTOs; re-verify in every Action/Handler.
7. Zod-validated forms with `useActionState`/`useFormStatus`.
8. `standalone` Docker images behind a reverse proxy; shared cache handler for multi-instance; consistent encryption + deployment IDs.
9. Pin to Next.js 16.x; adopt `cacheComponents` only after understanding explicit-caching implications.

- **Detailed `next/image`/`next/font` tuning, observability/APM, and rate-limiting specifics** were researched via search but not retained as verified citations due to source budget; treat vendor-specific performance checklists as follow-up verification, not as confirmed official guidance in this report.

- **No material contradictions** were found among the verified official sources; community folder-tree variants (`features/` vs `lib/` groupings) differ in naming but agree on the verified principles: thin routes, server-first reads, low client boundaries, and centralized server authorization.

# OpenCut Official Automation Interfaces — Current State

**Bottom line:** OpenCut currently provides **no stable, documented official automation interfaces**. The only official automation inventory is a **future roadmap for the ground-up rewrite**: Editor API, first-class third-party plugins, MCP server for AI agents, headless mode for automation/batch rendering, and an in-editor scripting tab. All are listed as “What’s coming,” with no endpoints, tools, auth, or usage documented.

## 1. What interfaces are officially listed?

OpenCut’s README states it “is being rewritten from the ground up” and lists as “What’s coming”:

- An Editor API
- First-class third party plugins (made possible by a plugin-first architecture)
- MCP server (for AI agents)
- Headless mode (automation, batch rendering)
- A scripting tab directly in the editor

Source: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)

No official REST API docs, CLI reference, MCP tool list, plugin SDK, webhook docs, or scripting guide were found. The live production site exposes only landing/projects/changelog/privacy/terms/contributor pages, with no automation/API section:

Source: [OpenCut official site](https://opencut.app)

Specifically **not found** as official offerings: public REST API, CLI, webhooks, or SDK beyond the roadmap labels above.

## 2. Capabilities, endpoints, auth, and usage

**None documented.**

- The roadmap provides only one-line labels — e.g. “MCP server (for AI agents)” and “Headless mode (automation, batch rendering)” — with no tool lists, endpoints, auth, or examples. Source: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)
- The rewrite repo’s `apps/api` is an internal placeholder, not an Editor/automation API. Its `src/index.ts` implements only `GET /`, `GET /health`, and `POST /echo`. Source: [apps/api/src/index.ts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/api/src/index.ts)
- A recursive tree of `main` shows only scaffolding (`apps/api`, `apps/desktop`, `apps/web`, `brand`, `changelog`) and no `mcp`, `plugin`, `headless`, `scripting`, CLI, webhook, or SDK paths. Source: [OpenCut repo file tree](https://api.github.com/repos/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/git/trees/main?recursive=1)

Do not confuse `apps/api` (`localhost:8787` dev service per README) with the planned Editor API — the former is currently just health/echo.

## 3. Status, version, and limitations

- **Status: unreleased / in design.** The README Contributing note says: “We’re not set up to take outside contributions yet while the architecture is being designed.” Source: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)
- **Current usable version is legacy:** the previous version at `opencut-classic` is described as “the one to reach for today,” while the main site still runs classic and the rewrite will live separately until ready to take over. Source: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)
- **Classic is archived:** the classic repo was archived May 17, 2026, is read-only, and is described as “Original OpenCut codebase” that is “archived and no longer maintained.” Source: [opencut-classic repo](https://github.com/opencut-app/opencut-classic)

Source: [OpenCut 0.3.0 changelog](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/changelog/0.3.0.md)

### Practical implication

If you need automation today, there is no official supported path (no stable API/CLI/MCP to build against). Track the rewrite repo for the Editor API / plugin-first architecture / MCP / headless / scripting milestones. Source: [OpenCut-app/OpenCut README](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut)

finalReport:
# Can you install a usable official OpenCut desktop app on macOS today? — No.

**Short answer:** There is no usable official OpenCut desktop application for macOS to download and install today. The official desktop target is an early, source-only developer build that opens only an empty window/shell with no editing features. Official guidance directs users to the classic web version at [opencut.app](https://opencut.app) instead.

## 1. Official distribution: no packaged macOS app

OpenCut describes itself as “a free and open source video editor for web, desktop, and mobile,” but the official site offers only “Try early beta” via `/projects`, with no macOS DMG, Mac App Store listing, or other desktop download button in the navigation/footer [opencut.app](https://opencut.app).

The canonical source repository confirms why:

> “OpenCut is being rewritten from the ground up... You can still find the previous version at opencut-app/opencut-classic, which is the one to reach for today. [opencut.app](https://opencut.app) still runs the classic version.” [Main README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)

The rewrite’s desktop folder is explicitly not a product release:

> “Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens.” [Desktop README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)

> “`apps/desktop/` is a new GPUI + Rust app. It is early: there is a `main.rs` and a working build setup, but no features yet.” [v0.3.0 Releases](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases)

Finding: no official packaged macOS OpenCut desktop app exists to download today; the only official desktop target is source-only.

## 2. macOS install method: source build only, no DMG / Homebrew / App Store

There is no documented DMG, Homebrew cask, or App Store install. Main development docs list only:

- install `proto`
- `proto use`
- `moon run web:dev`, `moon run api:dev`, `moon run desktop:dev — see apps/desktop/README.md` [Main README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)

Desktop-specific instructions are likewise only cargo/moon commands:

> “Rust is pinned in `.prototools` (`proto use` installs it). `moon run desktop:dev # cargo run`, `moon run desktop:check # cargo check`, `moon run desktop:build # cargo build --release`. The first build compiles GPUI from source and takes a while.” [Desktop README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)

### macOS requirements stated officially

- **Xcode command line tools (Metal renderer)** [Desktop README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)
- **Pinned toolchain:** `moon = "2.3.3"`, `bun = "1.3.11"`, `rust = "1.97.0"` [`.prototools`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/.prototools)

In practical terms on macOS you would need to clone `OpenCut-app/OpenCut`, install proto, run `proto use`, ensure Xcode CLT is installed, then `moon run desktop:dev` or `cargo build --release` — accepting a long first GPUI compile — and you still would not get an editor.

## 3. Usability: not usable — experimental shell only

All official status markers agree the desktop app is not usable as a video editor:

- Warning: “Very early. Right now this is just a window that opens.” [Desktop README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md)
- Release status: “only a `main.rs` and a working build setup, but no features yet.” [v0.3.0 Releases](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases)
- Code entry point only opens an `OpenCut`-titled GPUI window hosting `Shell::new(cx)`, with no editor implementation in `main` [main.rs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/src/main.rs)
- Project direction: rewrite in progress; classic/web is “the one to reach for today.” [Main README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md)

Therefore: even if you successfully compile it on macOS, you do not get timeline editing, import/export, effects, or other video-editor functionality.

## What to use instead today

If you need OpenCut functionality on macOS today, the official usable path is the web/classic version:

- Use [opencut.app](https://opencut.app) in a GPU-capable browser, or self-host/run `apps/web` from source per the main README [Main README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/README.md).
- Do not rely on third-party “OpenCut DMG” downloads claiming to be official — no such official artifact is documented in releases or docs.

## Limitations / uncertainty

- This assessment is based on official site, README, desktop README, release notes, pinned toolchain, and `main.rs` as of September 2026. Unofficial forks or community packaging were out of scope and were not validated.
- Future desktop releases could add packaged macOS builds; check [Releases](https://github.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/releases) and [Desktop README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/OpenCut-app/OpenCut/main/apps/desktop/README.md) for changes.
